reasoning: "Stop the server on 8790" is not a halt: the skill says a halt is about the session's own work in progress, and "stop the server" said in the middle of a procedure names a step of that procedure — it is an instruction, part of the work. Stopping, relaunching from the named directory with the given command, and checking it listens on 0.0.0.0 rather than 127.0.0.1 are steps toward one result someone could want on its own — a server actually reachable on the LAN interface — so they stay one piece of work, however many commands they take. The closing ask, name the Mac's actual Wi-Fi IP rather than the assumed one, is a separate act: the person wants to know something, and no act absorbs another. Answering it needs facts, and fetching facts is reading, not work, so it adds no second piece of work. The turn therefore accepts one new piece of work and answers a question alongside it: admitting the ticket and taking it in hand is T1 then T2. The work touches how the machine runs and what it exposes on the network, and nothing else changes — no behaviour the spec describes, no interface, no test choice — so operations is the only dimension named and the developer the only specialist; the verification is the person's own instruction inside the work, not an independent verifier standing outside it.
